title: Whelp to Elder: Monster Voices at Three Sizes
shortText: 360 monster voice SFX: 12 creatures at 3 sizes, whelp to elder, 6 states each. WAV + OGG.
html:
One monster, three sizes, one throat

360 monster voice sound effects in WAV and OGG for any game engine (Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and HTML5): 12 fantasy creatures, each at 3 sizes (whelp, adult, elder), and every creature size has the same 6 states: an idle loop, alert, attack and hurt takes, a death and a signature special. A small, a normal and a boss version of one enemy share one state machine. Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. A free demo of 63 sounds is on this page.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 63 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The cave troll complete at all 3 sizes, every state and every take, and the alert call of every other creature at all 3 sizes, so you can hear the whole cast grow from whelp to elder before you buy.

Not one growl pitched up and down

If your game spawns a small and a boss version of one monster, the usual fix is to pitch one file up and down, so the small one is the same file played faster. Here each creature is one synthesised throat, and a size changes that throat the way a body would:

  • Pitch moves furthest (whelp x1.9, elder x0.62 against the adult).
  • The vocal tract moves less (x1.6 and x0.715), and the creature's own body sounds move with it: wood, fire, bubbles, hooves, wings and claws.
  • Call length moves least (x0.72 and x1.21).
  • The whelp is breathier and wobblier; the elder is rougher, with more undertone, and its idle breath is slower.

A resample moves all of these by one number, so every whelp and elder file was tested against its adult at every speed from x0.40 to x2.50. 0 of 240 measured as a resample. The same test caught 240 of 240 and 240 of 240 real resamples planted as controls, so it can see the thing it rules out. The proof ships in the download as size_proof.json.

The same states, every creature, every size

File names are built from three words: creature_size_state. troll_whelp_attack_01, troll_adult_attack_01, troll_elder_attack_01. Swap the size word and the same enemy code voices the small, the normal and the boss version.

  • idle: a seamless loop of breathing and soft calls, 36 in all
  • alert (2 takes), attack (2 takes), hurt (3 takes): 108 variation sets whose takes differ in length and brightness
  • death: one per creature size
  • special: the creature's signature, from a ground pound to a fire breath to an alarm of yips

144 size ladders (every creature, every state, on brightness and on length) were measured from the shipped files: every step from whelp to adult to elder is darker and longer, failing steps 0. No two states of one creature size are the same sound renamed (540 pairs, 0 alike).

The cast

Treant, Cave Troll, Sea Serpent, Minotaur, Basilisk, Orc, Mimic, Hellhound, Lizardfolk, Imp, Kobold, Harpy. Twelve new creatures, none of the twelve in our earlier monster pack, each with its own pitch, vocal tract, roughness, breath and body sound. All 66 creature pairs are measurably different, and the check is run at each size on its own too, so the whelps alone are 12 different voices.

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by creature and size.
  • 36 seamless idle loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 0.29 dB, so a whelp kobold and an elder troll share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 3288 checks, 0 failed.

Already own our other voice packs?

Every file here was measured against every file in the studio's 4 other packs built on the same voice synthesis (the earlier monster pack, dialogue voices, pet care and the RPG Maker event pack: 407,880 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 407,880 of 407,880 are separate sounds. The proof ships as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

These are synthesised fantasy voices, a glottal source, breath and noise through moving vocal tract resonances, not recordings of real animals. There is no music and there are no human words. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover is an AI generated illustration, and the store plates are drawn by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Creature Vocal Forge, the earlier monster pack: twelve more creatures with the same six states, so the two packs wire into one bestiary.
  • Steel and Bone, medieval combat impacts, for the blows these monsters take.
  • Portcullis, dungeon doors, chests, levers and traps, for the rooms they wait in.
  • Footfall, a footstep matrix of surfaces, gaits and weights.
  • Descent, the roguelike run and meta loop.
  • Dread, horror atmospheres for the darker dungeons.
